* * *

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking
compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the pet

itioner is as follows:-
That on 11-02-2024 at about 8-30 p.m., the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-50- X-1271 from Malleshwaram towards K S Layout and when he reached near Sangolli Rayanna circle ie., near City Railway Station, Majestic area, Bangalore,
at that time the driver of Motor cab/car bearing Reg.no.KA-04- ED-2413 came from right side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and suddenly took the vehicle towards left side and hit to the hind portion of the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Sevakshethra Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He has aged about 63 years.
The petitioner was working as Real Estate Agent and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Motor cab/car bearing Reg.no.KA-04-ED-2413 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the insurer of Motor cab/car bearing Reg.no.KA-04-ED-2413 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license to drive the transport vehicle Srinivasa Rao H S vs Manjunatha R S on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42572905/
2 valid from 02-05-2018 to 01-05-2021, the accident was occurred on 11-02-2024, the vehicle involved in the accident is passenger carrying commercial vehicle and the said vehicle was not holding valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, as he was riding the motorcycle in a zig zag manner without taking any precautions and suddenly applied break in the middle of the main road and dashed to the insured car and that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding driving license and that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 11-02-2024 at about 8-30 pm., when he was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-50-X- 1271 from Malleshwaram towards K S Layout on G T road near Sangolli Rayanna circle, near to city Railway Station, Megestic area, Bangalore at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-ED-2413 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motorcycle.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or Award ?
8. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and three witnesses are examined as PW.2 to PW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P26.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 11-02-2024 at about 8-30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-50-X-1271 from Malleshwaram towards K S Layout and when he reached near Sangolli Rayanna circle ie., near City Railway Station, Majestic area, Bangalore, at that time Motor cab/car bearing Reg.no.KA-04-ED-2413 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came from right side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and suddenly took Srinivasa Rao H S vs Manjunatha R S on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42572905/
3 the vehicle towards left side and hit to the hind portion of the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R., Complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Srinivasa Rao H R, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0006/2024 by Chickpet Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
13.

Coming to the objection raised by the respondent no.2 as to delay in lodging the complaint is concerned, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 11-02-2024 at 08-30 pm., and the complaint came to be lodged on 12-02-2024 at 11-00 a.m., hence, there is less than one day delay in lodging the complaint.

Even if complaint is lodged on 12-02- 2024 but if the medical records are perused, on the date of accident itself the petitioner has taken treatment for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

Further when the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries, the family members will focus their attention in giving treatment to the injured and put their efforts to save the life of the injured instead of rushing to the police station to lodge the complaint.
Hence, delay of less than one day in lodging the compliant is not fatal to the case of the petitioner.

14. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, the police records discloses that due the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.

Further the PW.1 in his cross examination has clearly deposed that at the time of accident he was proceeding from Malleshwaram towards Kumara Swamy layout and when he reached near Sangolli Rayanna circle, at that time the offending vehicle which came from right side took the vehicle towards left side and hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though the learned counsel for respondent no.2 during the course of cross examination has posed suggestion that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner but nowhere suggested the manner in which according to them accident in question has occurred.
Even in the written statement also they have not stated the manner in which according to them accident has occurred.
Further the respondent no.2 has not examined the driver of their insured vehicle.
The respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained ex-parte.
Hence, there is no contra evidence from the respondents to say that the accident in question has not occurred in the manner stated by the petitioner.

Hence by considering the police records and the evidence of PW.,1 this court is of the opinion that the accident in question is due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate, Discharge summary and medical bills which are marked at Ex.P5, Ex.P9 to Ex.P21.
On going through the medical document it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Sevakshethra Hospital as an inpatient from 11-02-2024 to 11-03-2024.
Again the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Vasavi Hospitals for two times ie., from 06- 11-2024 to 08-11-2024, and from 07-02-2025 to 10-02- 2025.
Further he has produced inpatient bill for taking treatment at Trinity Hospital and Heart Foundation from 03-10-2024 to 05-10-2024.

Though the petitioner has produced the inpatient bill for the treatment taken at Trinity Hospital for the period 03-10-2024 to 05-10-2024 and has produced medical bill for Rs.35,000/- but the said treatment was taken for the heart disease from which the petitioner was suffering.

The PW.1 himself in his evidence has admitted that since 8 to 10 years he is suffering from diabetic and heart related disease and that earlier to the accident he had taken treatment at Manipal Hospital and after the accident he had taken treatment as inpatient for a period of 2 days at Trinity Hospital for diabetic and heart related treatment.
Further if Ex.P9 i.e.,
discharge

summary issued from Sevakshetra Hospital is perused, wherein it is clearly stated that the case of the petitioner is known case of diabetes mellitus since about 2008 he is on medication and hypertensive since 35 years and he has undergone stenting in Manipal Hospital.
Even the PW.4 who has assessed disability of petitioner has admitted that the petitioner undergone bypass surgery.

Hence, from the aforesaid evidence it can be said that the treatment taken by the petitioner at Trinity Hospital from 03-10- 2024 to 05-10-2024 is not related to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence, same cannot be considered.
If rest of the medical documents produced by the petitioner is considered, then it can be said that the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient in all for a period of 37 days.
If the medical documents and oral evidence of the PW.4 is perused, the petitioner underwent five surgeries.
As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is grievous in nature.
16. R Venkatesh -MRD Assistant at Sevakshethra Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him case sheet and x-rays are marked as Ex.P17 and Ex.P18.
17. Ravikumar G -Medical Record Manager at Vasavi Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.3 and through him 2 case sheets are marked as Ex.P23.

18. Dr. Arinash Parthasarathy - Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sreenivasa Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw.4 and through him Recent examination OP slip, Disability assessment Proforma and x-ray film are marked as Ex.P24 to Ex.P26.

PW.4 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 23-05-2025 for assessment of disability and that petitioner has suffered permanent physical impairment on left lower limb at 79% and to the whole body at 26%.
19.
If the cross examination of PW.4 is perused, he is not a treated doctor and except verifying the three discharge summaries he has not verified any other medical documents.
As per the own evidence of PW.4 the fracture injury is united and petitioner admitted for the second time for the reason of non union of fracture and infection in the fracture site.

It is further deposed that on 07-02-2025 implant was fixed and since prosthesis was implanted there is no need to remove the same and the petitioner is not taking any further treatment and all the treatment is now completed Srinivasa Rao H S vs Manjunatha R S on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42572905/
5 and there is no need to undergo any surgeries in future days.

sentences.text: 20. From the aforesaid evidence and from the medical records it can be gathered that the petitioner is diabetic and suffering from heart ailment.
It is true that petitioner has taken treatment for 37 days as inpatient and he has suffered grievous injury.

Hence, even though the petitioner has not suffered disability to the extent of 26% on whole body but the possibility of disability suffered by the petitioner due to the injuries sustained by him cannot be ruled out.

Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner at 20%.
21.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards pain and suffering.

23. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 87 medical bills for Rs.6,44,174/-, medical advance and bill paid receipts, 29 medical bills for sum of Rs.5,54,195/- and 2 advance receipts as per Ex.P13, 14, 20 and 21.
But as observed supra, the medical bills for Rs.35,000/-issued from Trinity Hospital is not related to the treatment taken by the petitioner for the injuries sustained in the accident.

Further if Ex.P20 is perused, the bill No. 3 for Rs.220/-
is for blood counting, bill no. 5 for Rs.999/- is for cardiology consultancy, bill no.7 for Rs.1250/- is for renal function (Kidney function test).
Hence, sum of Rs.35,000/- + Rs.220 + 999+ 1,250 has to be deducted out of Rs.11,98,369/-.
On such deduction the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner would come at around Rs.11,60,900/-.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.11,60,900/-.
24.

It is stated that petitioner was doing Real Estate Business and was earning sum of Rs.40,000/-
per month.
To substantiate the said contention the petitioner has not produced any materials.

In the absence of such document, this Tribunal considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
25.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment at Sevakshetra Hospital and Vasavi Hospitals.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 6 months as complete laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.99,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
26. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Sevakshetra Hospital and Vasavi Hospitals .
Further for 37 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental Srinivasa Rao H S vs Manjunatha R S on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42572905/
6 expenses is assessed at Rs.70,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of money during the year 2024.

sentences.text: 27. It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the petitioner was aged about 63 years.
In this regard, the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card/Ex.P.7 of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 15-10- 1961.
As the accident took place in the year 2024, therefore the petitioner was aged about 63 years as on the date of accident.

28 . So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.4 as he has assessed disability on higher side, this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 20% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 63 years, as per Sarla Varma's case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 61 to 65 is '7'.
So by applying the multiplier '9' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.2,77,200/- (i.e., 16,500 x 20% x 7 x 12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,77,200/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
29. The petitioner at his age of 63 years has suffered permanent disability, hence definitely some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities and discomfort would have caused to the petitioner.
Hence he is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 1,00,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 11,60,900/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 99,000/-
 laid up period 4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 70,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5

. Loss of Future Income Rs. 2,77,200/-
6. Loss of comfort and amenities Rs. 1,50,000/-
Total Rs

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.18,57,100/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakh Fifty Seven Thousand One Hundred only).
30.
As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.18,57,100/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakh Fifty Seven Thousand One Hundred only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
